articles.title: A Jewish couple’s art collection was looted by the Nazis in 1935; more than 90 years later, their heirs are still fighting over a Degas painting sold for $10.7 million
articles.summary: A pastel painting by French artist Edgar Degas has become the centre of a prolonged legal dispute over a Jewish couple's art collection looted by the
articles.body: A pastel painting by French artist Edgar Degas has become the centre of a prolonged legal dispute over a Jewish couple's art collection looted by the Nazis in 1935. The work, titled Danseuses, belonged to Margret and Ludwig Kainer before it was seized and sold during the Nazi era. After passing through art dealers and galleries in the international art market, the painting was sold privately for $6 million in 2009 before fetching $10.7 million at a Christie's auction in New York. The couple's purported heirs have challenged the transactions, arguing that their inheritance rights were overlooked. On June 4, 2026, a New York appellate court lifted a years-long pause on their lawsuit against Christie's, allowing the case to proceed.Nazis looted the Degas painting in 1935Danseuses was part of the art collection owned by Margret and Ludwig Kainer, a Jewish couple who left Germany in 1932 as the Nazi regime rose to power. In 1935, their collection, comprising more than 400 artworks, was looted by the Nazis and sold at an auction in Berlin on May 31 that year.The Degas painting subsequently passed through the international art market, with its documented history including dealers and galleries in London and Japan. Decades later, its ownership became the subject of a dispute involving the Kainers' purported heirs and a Swiss foundation that claimed rights to the family's assets.Who inherited the Kainers' estate?Ludwig Kainer died before his wife. Margret died in France in 1968 without children or a will, leaving questions about who was legally entitled to her estate.A Swiss foundation, Norbert Stiftung, later claimed rights to assets associated with the Kainer family. Its position relied partly on a German certificate of partial inheritance issued in 1972.People identifying themselves as Margret's heirs subsequently challenged the foundation's claim. They rely on French certificates of inheritance issued in 2012 and argue that they are the lawful successors to her estate.The purported heirs allege that UBS and its predecessors helped establish and control the foundation, which they say was wrongly treated as entitled to the family's assets.How the Degas painting sold for $10.7 millionIn 2009, Christie's facilitated an agreement with Norbert Stiftung under which the foundation relinquished its claim to the painting in exchange for a share of the proceeds.The painting was sold privately for $6 million in November 2009, with the foundation receiving $1.8 million under the agreement. Shortly afterwards, it was offered at Christie's auction in New York on November 3, 2009, where it fetched $10,722,500.The purported heirs argue that the transactions took place without their inheritance rights being properly recognised. They challenge the foundation's authority to relinquish its claim and have pursued legal action over the handling and sale of the painting.Why the heirs sued Christie'sThe purported heirs began legal proceedings in 2013 against UBS, Norbert Stiftung and Christie's. Their case centres on whether the foundation had legitimate rights to the painting and whether the transactions excluded the people who say they inherited Margret's estate.The heirs contend that Christie's helped facilitate the sale despite questions surrounding the foundation's claim. Christie's has disputed the plaintiffs' position that they are the lawful heirs entitled to pursue the case.In 2017, a New York court dismissed the claims against UBS and the foundation on jurisdictional grounds and paused the proceedings against Christie's while inheritance-related proceedings in Europe continued. The dismissals against UBS and the foundation were subsequently upheld on appeal, while the case against Christie's remained on hold.Why a New York court lifted the stay in 2026On June 4, 2026, New York's Appellate Division, First Department, ruled that the stay on the case against Christie's should be lifted. The decision, published as Estate of Margaret Kainer v Christie's Inc., 2026 NY Slip Op 03506, reversed a lower court's 2025 order and sent the matter back for further proceedings.The appellate court noted that the stay had lasted approximately nine and a half years. It expressed concern that further delays could make it increasingly difficult for the plaintiffs to reconstruct the events surrounding the 2009 transactions, particularly as some people involved had died or were elderly.The court also considered the lack of a clear timeline for the conclusion of the Swiss proceedings and the public interest in resolving claims involving Nazi-looted art fairly and without unnecessary delay.Where is the Degas painting now?The painting is listed in the Degas catalogue raisonné as belonging to a private collection. Its current owner and exact location have not been publicly identified in the available records.Its documented history includes the Kainers' collection in Germany, the 1935 Nazi-era auction, subsequent dealings through the international art market and the multimillion-dollar transactions in 2009.What happens next in the legal battle?The case against Christie's can now move forward in the New York trial court, where the parties may seek evidence relating to the painting's ownership history and the 2009 transactions.Key questions include whether the purported heirs are legally entitled to Margret Kainer's estate, whether Norbert Stiftung had authority to relinquish its claim to the painting, and whether Christie's bears legal responsibility in connection with the transactions.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2001, a Virginia road-widening plan cut through a 91-year-old carpenter’s farmhouse; VDOT bought it, sold the home back for $1, and the family arranged to move it 100 yards
articles.summary: In a unique arrangement, the Virginia Department of Transportation purchased a 91-year-old farmhouse in Fairfax County, allowing the owner to buy it back for just $1, ensuring its preservation amidst road-widening efforts.
articles.body: In a peculiar road-widening project in Fairfax County, Virginia, in 2001, the Virginia Department of Transportation (VDOT) purchased a farmhouse and sold it back to its owner for $1. According to the Washington Post, Raymond Demory, who built the two-storey house in the 1930s, faced the prospect of losing the home where he raised his family. The farmhouse was allowed to be preserved, but the family was left responsible for moving it, and the cost of moving it exceeded the compensation received.The relocation consisted of a wider plan to widen an eight-mile section of Route 123 situated between Burke Lake Road and Route 1 in Occoquan. Also known as the Ox Road, it changed considerably since Demory built his farmhouse beside what was then a dirt thoroughfare. The property stood along a congested route, and the proposed expansion required land from his 11-acre holding. Negotiations lasted more than a year before the parties reached an arrangement that saved the house from being demolished.How the property deal was negotiatedThe disagreement stemmed from the amount that was offered to the family and other alternatives made available to the family. The Post reported that the Virginia Department of Transportation (VDOT) had offered approximately $150,000 for the farmhouse. Demory's granddaughter, Carol Christoforatos, who held the legal authority to manage his affairs, believed the farmhouse property, which included a detached three-car garage, a work shed, and two acres of land, was worth about $300,000 and rejected the initial offer.Subsequently, the department proposed re-engineering of the road so that it would pass by in front of the house. However, Christoforatos harboured qualms that the arrangement left the building dangerously close to traffic and would put the family in a position where they would have to pay rent to the state. This prompted her to tell the department that the family would prefer to have the farmhouse moved.The final agreement boiled down to state transport officials purchasing the house and two acres only to sell it back to Demory for $1. The arrangement separated ownership of the structure from the land transaction and left the family responsible for relocating the house farther back on the property. The reported compensation was $239,000, rather than the approximately $150,000 that was offered initially.The cost of preserving the farmhouseAlthough the agreement was instrumental in preserving the building, it didn’t abate the problems caused by the road project, as Christoforatos said the relocation was more costly in comparison to the $239,000 received. She also noted that the talks, along with the logistical challenges of relocating an elderly resident's home, brought considerable stress.Demory had already moved into an assisted-living facility in Prince William County and had planned to stay there until the farmhouse’s relocation was completed. On June 8, 2001, the building was scheduled to be lifted and moved approximately 100 yards from its original position under permissible weather conditions. Fairfax County supervisor Elaine N. McConnell, who had advocated widening Route 123 for years, helped negotiate the agreement and credited the department with saving the house, despite the criticism the department faced over property acquisitions.On the other hand, the department declined to elaborate on the discussion and maintained it had worked with the family to resolve the dispute, although the outcome failed to pacify their dissatisfaction or the relocation costs. The agreement provided an alternative to demolishing the farmhouse, but the report did not confirm the move on the scheduled date or the outcome of the physical relocation.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1929, World War I veteran Harry Andrews began building Ohio’s Loveland Castle by hand; 50 years later, his knights still run it as a museum
articles.summary: Explore Loveland Castle, a unique museum in Ohio built by WWI veteran Harry Andrews over 50 years, now maintained by his brotherhood of knights.
articles.body: Loveland Castle, known formally as Château Laroche, sits on the banks of the Little Miami River just north of the village of Loveland, Ohio, in Symmes Township, northeast of Cincinnati. A narrow, winding road drops down a hill to reach it. The stone building at the bottom looks out of place among the wooded river valley and the suburbs nearby. The castle operates as a museum run by volunteer knights, members of a brotherhood who take no vows except the Ten Commandments. Harry Delos Andrews built most of the property himself.Harry Andrews as an Army medic, a 1918 meningitis diagnosis and a return to OhioThe SPACES archive records that Andrews was born in 1890 and served in the US Army as a medic in World War I. Andrews reportedly suffered from spinal meningitis and was mistakenly declared dead in 1918, although he was still alive. According to the account, the mistake went uncorrected for about six months, and during that time his fiancée married someone else. He remained single for the rest of his life. According to Roadside America, he stayed in Europe after the war to see the castles. In Ohio, he used to work for a local newspaper and taught a Sunday school class for boys.The Knights of the Golden Trail and the lots Andrews bought in 1927A museum guide at mnmuseumofthems.org says Andrews formed an imaginary club for the boys in his class and called it the Knights of the Golden Trail. Boys swore that they would keep their promise of observing the Ten Commandments and stay away from the allurements of modern-day urban living. According to the castle’s official history, the parents of one of the Sunday school boys obtained riverfront land through a newspaper promotion and later sold it to Andrews and the Knights. The museum guide at mnmuseumofthems.org gives 1927 as the year Andrews purchased the land. Accounts differ on which newspaper ran the promotion. According to Roadtrippers, one account says that in the 1920s, The Cincinnati Enquirer offered riverside lots to readers who prepaid for a one-year subscription, and that Andrews acquired 11 lots this way, on which he later built the castle.The official history gives a different version, saying the promotion came from the Cincinnati Business Courier with a six-month prepaid subscription. Roadside America’s page on Château Laroche reports that Andrews kept a tally of his construction work, recording 2,600 sacks of cement, 32,000 quart-sized milk cartons used to make concrete bricks, 54,000 five-gallon buckets of dirt, and 56,000 pailfuls of stone. As the buildings looked like towers, Andrews thought that knights needed a castle.Construction began on June 5, 1929, with river stone and 32,000 milk carton bricksAndrews began building Château Laroche on June 5, 1929, according to the official Loveland Castle website. Initially, Andrews employed limestone from the Little Miami River. When this resource was exhausted, he started making concrete bricks out of quart milk cartons. Andrews kept a tally of what went into the structure, which Roadside America reproduces: 2,600 sacks of cement, 32,000 quart-sized milk cartons used to make concrete bricks, 54,000 five-gallon buckets of dirt, and 56,000 pailfuls of stone. The SPACES record says the finished structure took fifty years of labor, most of it done by Andrews himself. It comprised watchtowers, terraces, a banquet hall, a dry moat, and a dungeon.The official Loveland Castle website and Atlas Obscura both describe a secret room that stayed a mystery until it crumbled from neglect, years after Andrews’ death. According to Roadtrippers, the stones in the walls of the upper floor chapel were collected on trips and given as gifts by Andrews’ admirers from around the world.Andrews’s death in April 1981 and the Knights who run the museum todayThe latter part of Andrews’s life was tough. Roadside America mentions that Andrews was the target of thieves, vandalism, and nocturnal harassment at the castle. Andrews was said to arm himself for protection. Roadtrippers reports that Andrews suffered severe burns while trying to extinguish a rubbish fire on the castle grounds in March 1981 and died a few days later. Andrews has bequeathed the castle to the Knights of the Golden Trail, who continue the maintenance of the castle and use it as a museum and tourist attraction. The official website indicates that their operating hours are 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM during April 1- September 30, and weekends only from October 1 - March 31. The castle is open from 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM from April 1 to September 30, and on weekends only from October 1 to March 31. Admission is $5 per person, and children aged 5 and under enter free, according to the official Loveland Castle website.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Storm Austen: Strong 70mph winds could hit south Wales on Friday
articles.summary: Gusts of wind about 50 to 60mph are likely to hit large parts of south Wales on Friday.
articles.body:
Travel disruption and damage to buildings are expected when Storm Austen, the first named storm of the autumn , hits south Wales later this week.

The Met Office said the storm will bring a spell of strong winds up to 70mph (112km/h) overnight on Thursday and into Friday, mainly in coastal areas.

The yellow warning for Wales was issued on Wednesday morning, with periods of heavy rain also expected. The Met Office said injuries and danger to life from flying debris are possible.

Some roads and bridges may close, and longer journey times and cancellations to public transport are possible.

The weather warning is in place between 00:00 and 14:00 BST on Friday.

The Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) has urged anyone visiting the coast in south Wales to "to stay vigilant and not take unnecessary risks".

Gusts of wind about 50 to 60mph are likely to hit areas such as Cardiff, Swansea and Merthyr Tydfil.

Some coastal or exposed areas could see about 70mph gusts of wind, the Met Office said, adding winds will slowly ease during Friday afternoon.

Ross Macleod, RNLI water safety manager, said: "If you plan to visit the coast or a waterside location, we urge you stay a safe distance from the water as conditions could knock you off your feet or wash you into the sea."

MacLeod said anyone in trouble in the water should "lie back in the water with your head so far back that your ears are wet, extend your arms and legs and try to relax as best as you can until you get control of your breathing before then calling for help or swimming to safety".

He added if anyone sees someone in danger, throw them something buoyant into the water and call 999 or 112 and ask for the coastguard.

articles.title: 'Stupid comments': Macron slams Trump for using France unrest for midterm campaign
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday slammed world leaders for \"campaigning behind France's back\" with their remarks on the ongoing nationwide
articles.body: French President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday slammed world leaders for "campaigning behind France's back" with their remarks on the ongoing nationwide protests over rising living costs and deteriorating school conditions.Without naming US President Donald Trump, Macron said France was already dealing with difficulties and did not need foreign leaders using its problems for their election campaigns."We are already dealing with difficulties, we do not need foreign leaders using our problems for their election campaigns," Macron said."There has been foreign manipulation of information afterward — that is certain. This led to unacceptable and downright stupid comments from many people, including foreign leaders," he added."We have seen artificial-intelligence-generated images showing scenes that never happened in France. People have claimed that we were invaded by hordes of migrants and Islamists, which is completely false," he further said.This comes after Trump invoked violent unrest in France to attack political opponents and rally support for Republicans, warning that similar scenes could unfold in the United States if his political opponents prevail in the November 3 midterm elections.Trump claimed he had warned French President Emmanuel Macron to close France's borders, saying Paris would otherwise become a "Muslim city".At a rally on Monday evening, Trump blamed immigration for the unrest in France, where protests over rising living costs and declining purchasing power escalated into looting and clashes with police in several cities, according to Reuters."If you want to see what is at stake in this election, just look at what's happening in France," Trump told the crowd.Nationwide demonstrations in France were called over the cost of living and pressure on household purchasing power. articles.title: Mike Tyson’s co-founded company seeks $10 million from Hulk Hogan’s estate over a beer brand deal; the claim is double the wrestler’s reported $5 million probate estate
articles.summary: A company co-founded by Mike Tyson is pursuing a $10 million claim against Hulk Hogan's estate over a celebrity beer brand deal.
articles.body: A company co-founded by Mike Tyson is pursuing a $10 million claim against Hulk Hogan's estate over a celebrity beer brand deal. Carma HoldCo, a celebrity licensing and branding company, filed the breach of contract claim in Florida over Real American Beer, saying it was cut out of the partnership. Those accused of wrongdoing deny all the allegations. If you are searching for clear answers about the Real American Beer lawsuit, this guide explains who is claiming what, how the brand's story unfolded, what the defendants say in reply, and what the outcome could mean for Hogan's family and legacy.How a company co-founded by Mike Tyson came to claim $10 million from Hulk Hogan's estate in FloridaCarma HoldCo is a holding company that specialises in celebrity licensing and branding, and Mike Tyson is among its co-founders. On 20 January 2026, the company filed court documents in Florida saying Hulk Hogan's estate owed it $10 million immediately for breach of contract and other claims, according to Us Weekly. The publication reports that Carma says Real American Beer copied its idea, and that lawyers for the estate had yet to respond when the claim was reported. At the centre of the dispute is the brand with which Hogan was associated before he died on 24 July 2025, aged 71. Because Hogan has died, the demand for immediate payment is directed at the estate that now manages the assets he left behind.What Carma HoldCo alleges about Real American Beer and the earlier federal lawsuit filed in ChicagoThe claim in Florida follows an earlier fight. In July 2025, Carma sued a former president and a former chief legal and licensing officer in federal court in Chicago. The company accused them of poaching Hogan by using its ideas for the beer brand. The lawsuit alleges that Hogan was a brand ambassador for Carma when a separate company launched the beer line. Carma says former employees used stolen materials to pitch that rival company, and the complaint seeks damages of at least $10 million. Put simply, Carma's case is that the Real American Beer concept began with its work and was then taken elsewhere, leaving it without a share of the deal and now looking to Hogan's estate for payment.What the people accused in the earlier lawsuit say in reply and how Real American Beer reached the marketThose named in the Chicago lawsuit reject Carma's version of events. NewsNation reports that the defendants say Carma never developed or contracted for a beer, had no agreement with Hogan, and owned no beer-related trade secrets. They also say they neither solicited Hogan nor interfered with any contract or relationship he had. In plain terms, the dispute turns on whether Carma held an enforceable agreement or protectable ideas, which the defendants insist it did not. The brand is not new: the brand's website says Real American Beer officially launched in June 2024 and is available in 20 states. That timeline means the product was on sale for more than a year before Hogan died on 24 July 2025, so Carma's claim asks a court to look back at how an established beer brand came to be tied to the wrestler.What the $10 million claim could mean for the roughly $5 million estate Hulk Hogan left to his son NickThe size of the demand matters when set against what Hogan left. Ridley Law reports that his will was signed in 2016 and amended several times through 2023, naming his son Nick as sole beneficiary of an estate that went through probate and was valued at about $5 million. That filing listed $200,000 in cryptocurrency, $799,000 in personal and intellectual property, and a right of publicity valued at $4 million. A $10 million claim would be twice that probate figure, although a probate filing lists only property held in a person's own name, while trusts stay private. The same analysis found no sign of a dispute over who inherits under the will, so the beer claim concerns what the estate may owe, not who receives it.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: MNEK cancels tour over lack of ticket sales and production costs
articles.summary: The Grammy-nominated artist was due to start a run of shows for his latest album Bulldozer!! next month.
articles.body:
MNEK has cancelled his upcoming tour due to a lack of ticket sales and the show not being "ready to the standard" he wanted.

The Grammy-nominated artist, who has worked with the likes of Beyoncé, Zara Larsson and Madonna, was due to start a run of shows for his latest album Bulldozer!! next month.

In a statement shared on Instagram, the 31-year-old said he joins other artists who have cancelled shows recently as a result of "high production costs" and "over-ambitious planning".

Earlier this year, The Pussycat Dolls called off almost the entire US leg of their reunion tour following poor ticket sales.

The singer, whose real name is Uzoechi Emenike, said he had been "really looking forward" to performing his new album but had "no interest in doing this tour if I can't do it right".

He thanked fans who had bought tickets and said they would be refunded soon.

The artist also said he would try to tour the album when he could put on a show which fans "deserve".

Pop star Larsson, whose hit album Midnight Sun was executive produced by MNEK, was among those who offered their support to the artist in the comments.

Little Mix star Leigh-Anne Pinnock also sent him love, while singer Becky Hill encouraged him, saying: "Touring is devastatingly expensive but you'll find a way".

A growing number of artists have reported struggling with a "cost of touring crisis" due to rising prices.

Earlier this year, the chair of the Featured Artists Coalition and Blur drummer David Rowntree told the BBC is was "virtually impossible now to make touring pay for itself" .

MNEK had been due to play dates across the UK and Europe, with tickets starting from about £30.

Born in south-east London, he became a professional songwriter at the age of 14 when he signed his first publishing deal.

He went on to co-write for British acts such as The Saturdays and Little Mix and later earned credits on tracks for global stars like Madonna, Kylie Minogue and Christina Aguilera.

His first Grammy nomination came in 2014 for his collaboration track, Need U (100%), with Duke Dumont and A*M*E.

He was also nominated earlier this year for best dance pop recording for his work on Midnight Sun.

After years as a featured artist, he broke out in his own right to release his debut studio album Language in 2018.

Fans have had to wait eight years for the follow-up, with his second album Bulldozer!! finally released last month.

articles.title: Dave Bautista worked as a bouncer and borrowed money for his daughters’ Christmas gifts before becoming a WWE star; he later built a second career as a Hollywood actor
articles.summary: Before becoming a WWE champion and a familiar face in Hollywood, Dave Bautista faced a period of financial struggle that forced him to reconsider his
articles.body: Before becoming a WWE champion and a familiar face in Hollywood, Dave Bautista faced a period of financial struggle that forced him to reconsider his future. In his late 20s, he was working as a nightclub bouncer in Washington, DC, when he realised he could not afford Christmas presents for his two daughters. Bautista later recalled asking his employer at the club to lend him money, an experience that left him ashamed and determined to change his circumstances. At around 30, he began pursuing professional wrestling, despite an unsuccessful first tryout. The decision eventually transformed his life, taking him from nightclub security to the wrestling ring and, later, to a second career as an actor.Dave Bautista’s struggle to afford Christmas gifts for his daughtersBautista spent more than a decade working as a bouncer, a job that provided an income but left him without the financial security he wanted for his family. He left school at 17 and has spoken openly about having little formal education or a clear career path to fall back on. The Christmas when he could not afford gifts for his daughters became a turning point. In a 2023 interview with British GQ, he recalled asking a man he worked for at a club to borrow money. The experience made him confront the fact that he needed to pursue a different future.He faced rejection before entering WWEBautista initially tried out for World Championship Wrestling, hoping his years of weightlifting and athletic training would help him secure a contract. Instead, he was rejected after a gruelling tryout. He later enrolled at the Wild Samoan Training Center in Pennsylvania to learn professional wrestling. Although he struggled with the speaking and performance aspects of the sport at first, he continued training and eventually secured a developmental contract with the World Wrestling Federation, now known as WWE, in 2000. He made his main-roster debut in 2002 under the ring name Batista and gradually established himself as one of the promotion’s leading performers.How Batista became a WWE championBautista’s breakthrough came as part of Evolution, a prominent wrestling faction that also included Triple H, Ric Flair and Randy Orton. His rise culminated in 2005, when he won the Royal Rumble and defeated Triple H at WrestleMania 21 to capture the World Heavyweight Championship. Over his wrestling career, he won six world championships and became one of WWE’s major stars. He left WWE in 2010 to pursue acting, returned for a period in 2014 and made another comeback in 2019 before retiring following WrestleMania 35.Transition from wrestling to HollywoodActing became Bautista’s next major challenge. After leaving WWE, he pursued film roles, initially taking smaller parts while learning the craft. His breakthrough arrived in 2014 when he played Drax the Destroyer in Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy. The role introduced him to a much wider international audience and helped establish him as more than a wrestler making occasional film appearances. He went on to appear in films including Spectre, Blade Runner 2049, Dune and Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery.Why Dave Bautista wants to be taken seriously as an actorAlthough his physical presence helped make him a successful wrestler and action-film performer, Bautista has said he wants to be judged on his acting rather than simply his size or fame. In interviews, he has described acting as a craft he is committed to improving and has spoken about seeking roles that challenge him. His filmography spans science fiction, action, mystery and drama, allowing him to work with filmmakers beyond the wrestling world.His transition to Hollywood was not without setbacks. After leaving WWE, he struggled to find steady acting work, spent much of his wrestling earnings and lost his house to foreclosure. He also sold cars and motorcycles before rebuilding his career. The success of Guardians of the Galaxy helped change his fortunes, but Bautista has continued to pursue roles that broaden his range rather than relying solely on his established wrestling persona.You use AI every day. articles.summary: LUCKNOW: The Nagpur court on Wednesday granted three-day transit remand to the Uttar Pradesh Police for Shraddha Dubey and two other accused in the murder
articles.body: LUCKNOW: The Nagpur court on Wednesday granted three-day transit remand to the Uttar Pradesh Police for Shraddha Dubey and two other accused in the murder case of Shiva Sharma. Police have left for Lucknow with all three.Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and their driver Danish were arrested on Tuesday in a joint operation by the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (UPSTF) and Lucknow Police.The three accused had been absconding, with a reward of Rs 50,000 announced for each of them. They were apprehended after intensive raids at multiple locations.A murder case was registered at the Hazratganj police station on October 9 under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), following a written complaint filed by the victim's mother, Ranjana Sharma.Lucknow Police had initially announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to the accused, which was later increased to Rs 50,000. Specialised teams, including surveillance units, the Special Operations Group (SOG) and local police, were deployed to trace them.On Tuesday, following the arrest of the three absconding accused, Ranjana Sharma expressed gratitude to the police, the Special Task Force and Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath.She described the arrests as the "first step toward justice" on the day of Vijayadashami.Speaking to ANI, Ranjana said the case would now proceed according to due process of law and expressed faith that justice would be served."I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to everyone— the police, the STF, the administration, CM Yogi Adityanath, and all those who supported us. It is significant that today is the day of Vijayadashami, and this marks the first step toward justice for Shiva. Following this arrest, the case will proceed according to the due process of law. As for the harassment, there are many other videos currently in people's possession. I have full faith that justice will be served," she said.Uttar Pradesh additional director general of police (Law and Order) Amitabh Yash said Shraddha Dubey had evaded arrest by consistently wearing a burqa, minimising her use of communication devices, limiting interactions and staying in low-end hotels with minimal surveillance."She will now be brought to Lucknow on transit remand, where the Lucknow Police will conduct interrogations and advance the investigation. To evade the police and remain on the run, she consistently wore a burqa, minimized the use of communication devices, and kept her interactions with others to an absolute minimum. She chose to stay in low-end hotels—places with minimal surveillance and less police oversight," he told reporters.Yash also said police had received information that Shraddha Dubey had gone to Nepal before returning. articles.title: Bristol UWE student who murdered housemate jailed for life
articles.summary: Jamie Collins, 21, was ambushed and killed in the garden of the home he shared with his killer.
articles.body:
A student has been jailed for life with a minimum term of 28 years for murdering his university housemate after lying in wait and stabbing him 30 times.

Zack Coughlan, 23, ambushed Jamie Collins, 21, in the garden of their home near Bristol on 8 April and left him dying in the alleyway to dispose of bloodstained evidence. He called police eight hours later.

Coughlan had denied murder and a trial was under way at Bristol Crown Court but he changed his plea to guilty on Tuesday .

In a statement read in court, Collins' step-mother Lisa Jane Collins said his death had "affected our family in a deep, lasting and profound way. From now on, we will always be the couple whose boy got murdered".

Both men were final-year University of the West of England (UWE) students and lived together in a house in Filton.

Collins only had two pieces of coursework to complete before he would have returned home to his family in Swansea, where his dad already had an engineering job set up for him.

Lisa added that police came to their house early in the morning after the attack, to inform them of their son's death.

"We had the horror of waking up his siblings to tell them their brother Jamie had been killed, even though we had very little information," Lisa said.

Lisa added that Collins' father Rob was incapable of working due to stress and his business went under, leaving him in debt.

"Listening to the over-performative drama of Zack's evidence was excruciating as he made himself out to be the victim," Lisa added.

"I found it physically distressing being at the trial, I have vomited twice after hearing about the brutality."

During sentencing, Judge Justice Linden told Coughlan: "Collins was an idealist who took an interest in the problems of the world and society.

"It comes with great shock that anyone could do what you chose to do to him.

"I'm sure you were planning to kill Collins and had been for some time.

"Your guilty plea came at a point in the trial when your conviction was inevitable."

During the trial, Coughlan claimed he was fearful of Collins, saying he had threatened to kill him and therefore he had "no choice" but to wait for his housemate to return from university and stab him repeatedly.

Judge Linden said: "I do not accept your evidence that he did or said anything that made you believe he would be violent towards you in any way.

"Your evidence about these conversations was at odds with other evidence about Collins, that he was a gentle soul who was averse to conflict and confrontation ."

After the attack, Coughlan left his housemate to die in the alleyway behind the house they shared before cycling away on the victim's bike.

On returning home, Coughlan ate pizza and played video games, claiming he "had to disconnect" from what happened. He did not call 999 for another five hours.

The entire attack was caught on CCTV, which jurors heard Coughlan later rewatched five times.

Det Ch Insp Lucy Edgeworth, of the major crime investigation team, said "all the evidence suggests" the killing was a "pre-planned, cold-blooded execution".

She said despite Coughlan claiming his housemate's political views had become more extreme and that he had talked about killing Coughlan, the motive for the murder was "not clear".

"We know there was a dispute about rent. We know that they held different political views.

"But none of those things make any sense to why somebody would carry out such a horrific crime," she said.

articles.title: In the late 1950s, guitarist Lonnie Mack began using one of the earliest Gibson Flying V guitars; after decades of concerts and recordings, his famous 'Number 7' and an amplifier sold together for $550,000 in 2026
articles.summary: A guitar associated with blues-rock pioneer Lonnie Mack has sold for $550,000 as part of a lot that included the amplifier that helped shape his
articles.body: A guitar associated with blues-rock pioneer Lonnie Mack has sold for $550,000 as part of a lot that included the amplifier that helped shape his distinctive sound. The instrument, a 1958 Gibson Flying V known as “Number 7”, was auctioned by Heritage Auctions on October 15, 2026. According to the auction house’s October 16 announcement, the sale included Mack’s 1962 Magnatone Custom 440 amplifier and his recognisable leather stage strap. The guitar accompanied Mack through decades of performances and recordings, becoming closely identified with his career. Its auction result reflects both the instrument’s rarity and its connection to a musician whose playing influenced generations of guitarists.How ‘Number 7’ became Mack’s signature guitarMack began using the Gibson Flying V in the late 1950s, when its unusual angular design stood apart from conventional electric guitars. The instrument earned its nickname because Mack said it was the seventh guitar to leave the production line when Gibson introduced the model, according to Heritage Auctions.The Flying V had initially struggled commercially. Fewer than 100 examples were sold during its first two years of production, according to Heritage Auctions. Its arrow-shaped body was visually striking but could be awkward to play while seated. Mack was among the musicians who recognised its potential, alongside blues guitarist Albert King and the Kinks’ Dave Davies.For Mack, the instrument became more than a stage accessory. Its distinctive appearance made it a recurring feature of photographs, album covers and performances throughout his career. Rolling Stone later included “Number 7” on its 2019 list of 20 iconic guitars.The modifications that helped create his soundMack adapted the guitar to suit his playing style. He had a guitar shop owner install a Bigsby tremolo arm, which required a steel support bar fitted between the Flying V’s two wings. The device allowed him to alter the pitch of notes and add expressive movement to his playing. His creative use of the tremolo arm became associated with his instrumental hit “Wham!” and helped popularise the term “whammy bar,” a name still widely used for the device.Mack combined blues and country fingerpicking with a style often described as blue-eyed soul. After session work in the late 1950s and early 1960s, he recorded “Memphis,” a version of Chuck Berry’s instrumental, and “Wham!”, an original composition for Fraternity Records. Both became hits and featured prominently on his 1963 debut album, The Wham of That Memphis Man. These recordings helped establish Mack as an influential early blues-rock guitarist. His Flying V and its modified hardware became central to the sound that distinguished him from other players.Guitar and amplifier sold togetherThe $550,000 auction lot paired “Number 7” with Mack’s 1962 Magnatone Custom 440 amplifier, which Heritage described as an essential part of his signature guitar tone. The package also included his recognisable leather stage strap.According to Heritage’s September auction announcement, the guitar had not undergone further alterations since Mack’s death. It came with its original tuners, another period-correct set and the updated tuners he used during his career. The guitar’s history, customised features and association with Mack added to the significance of the auction lot. Aaron Piscopo, Heritage Auctions’ director of vintage guitars and musical instruments, described it as one of the defining instruments of early blues-rock guitar.A record-setting auction for vintage instrumentsMack’s guitar was among the headline lots in Heritage Auctions’ October 15 sale, which included 201 lots and attracted 848 international bidders. The auction generated $2.15 million overall. Another major result came from a 1959 Gibson Les Paul Standard Sunburst, which sold for $781,250. Heritage said it set a world auction record for a vintage guitar without celebrity provenance. The exceptionally preserved instrument retained its original finish, pickups and other components.The two sales highlighted different reasons collectors value historic guitars. The Les Paul attracted attention for its originality and condition, while “Number 7” carried a direct connection to a musician and the development of blues-rock guitar. For Mack’s Flying V, the $550,000 result placed a piece of musical history in the spotlight, recognising an instrument that helped define his career and left a lasting mark on electric guitar playing.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tapir born on Isle of Man dies following illness
articles.summary: Zeus, an 11-year-old tapir born on the Isle of Man died following a short illness.
articles.body:
A tapir at Curraghs Wildlife Park has died after a short illness.

The 'much-loved' animal, called Zeus, was born on the Isle of Man 11 years ago and was the only male tapir at the park.

Park manager Kathleen Graham said the animal, which died of colic, was popular among visitors and will be missed.

"Losing an animal is always difficult, both for the people who care for them and for those who have come to know them during visits," she said.

"Visitors may notice that the paddock beside the jumping pillow, where Zeus lived, is now empty. This space will remain so for the time being," she said.

Following Zeus's death, Kathleen believes the park may make a donation towards a tapir conservation project.

"When red panda Kush passed away, we gave a substantial donation to the Red Panda Network. So I would imagine that when our conservation team meets we will probably discuss doing a donation in his honour," Kathleen said.

She added: "It is always hard to say goodbye to a favourite animal but we are aware there are a number of very wise animals here that still need our care and attention.

articles.title: About 30 years after a London taxi driver paid £40 for an old painting at a car boot sale, experts linked it to 19th-century Amritsar and the work sold for £75,000 at a 2016 auction
articles.summary: A painting bought for just £40 at a car boot sale in Britain turned out to be a remarkable piece of Indian art nearly three decades later.
articles.body: A painting bought for just £40 at a car boot sale in Britain turned out to be a remarkable piece of Indian art nearly three decades later. According to Antiques Trade Gazette, which documented the discovery in its 50 Great Objects collection, the painting sold for £75,000, excluding the buyer’s premium, at Roseberys in London on April 15, 2016. Initially catalogued with a modest estimate of £500 to £1,000, the work attracted intense bidding after specialists identified its subject as the historic walled city of Amritsar, with the Golden Temple in the background. Its possible artist was also linked to the city’s 19th-century artistic tradition.A £40 purchase that remained unnoticed for decadesThe painting belonged to a London taxi driver who had purchased it at a car boot sale around 30 years before the auction. The seller had initially asked £60, but the driver negotiated the price down to £40. For years, the painting remained an ordinary second-hand purchase rather than a recognised work of historical importance. Its significance only became apparent when it was brought to the attention of the art market and examined by specialists.Roseberys offered the work in a specialist sale of Islamic and Indian art, giving it an estimate of £500 to £1,000. Despite the modest valuation, the painting attracted multiple bidders, with competition eventually pushing the price to £75,000, excluding the buyer’s premium of 23%. The result was far beyond the original estimate and transformed the driver’s inexpensive purchase into a valuable auction discovery.Painting depicted the historic city of AmritsarThe painting was a large Indian gouache miniature on paper, measuring approximately 59 by 85 centimetres. Its crowded composition depicted the walled old city of Amritsar, with the Golden Temple, also known as Harmandir Sahib, visible in the background. The Golden Temple is the holiest religious complex in Sikhism, making the painting’s subject particularly significant. Rather than presenting only a single building or a formal religious scene, the work captured a bustling urban setting filled with people and architectural details.One of its most intriguing features was a small self-portrait believed to show the artist at work. In the upper-left portion of the composition, a figure can be seen painting a portrait inside an architectural alcove. This detail added another layer of interest to the painting, connecting its creator directly with the scene being depicted. The combination of the cityscape, religious landmark and numerous human figures offered a glimpse into the artistic representation of 19th-century Amritsar.Artist may have been Baba Bishan SinghSpecialists attributed the painting tentatively to Baba Bishan Singh, an artist who lived from 1836 to around 1900. He belonged to a family of painters working in Lahore and Amritsar during the second half of the 19th century. According to Antiques Trade Gazette, the family was involved in maintaining the murals and decorative motifs on the walls of the Golden Temple. This connection made the possible attribution especially relevant to the painting’s subject.According to Antiques Trade Gazette, Bishan Singh participated in the 1864 exhibition of arts and crafts in Lahore, where he displayed 10 pictures. These included depictions of the courts of Maharaja Ranjit Singh and Sher Singh, as well as the Municipal Committee of Amritsar. The exhibition attracted the attention of Robert Baden-Powell, who later commented on Bishan Singh’s work in his Handbook of the Manufactures and Arts of the Punjab. He noted weaknesses in the perspective of the buildings but praised the quality of the figure drawing.The possibility that the newly discovered painting was among the works shown in Lahore in 1864 adds historical interest, although the connection has not been established conclusively.Auction specialist delivered unexpected newsThe £75,000 result was an extraordinary outcome for the vendor, who had paid only £40 for the painting decades earlier. According to Antiques Trade Gazette, specialist Peter Greenway contacted the taxi driver after the sale to tell him the result. The driver reportedly told Greenway that he had been having a difficult day because his taxi had suffered a flat tyre, preventing him from going to work. After hearing the auction news, he decided to give himself the weekend off.The story became a memorable example of how an overlooked object bought second-hand can turn out to have considerable artistic and historical importance. The painting’s journey from a car boot sale to a specialist auction also illustrates the role of expert research in identifying works that have been miscatalogued or remained unrecognised for years. Its final price reflected not simply the difference between £40 and £75,000, but the discovery of a potentially important record of Amritsar’s artistic and urban history.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'All of Us Are Dead Season 2': When and where to watch the Korean zombie thriller; All you need to know about the new cast, characters and more
articles.summary: The wait for 'All of Us Are Dead Season 2' is finally coming to an end.
articles.body: The wait for 'All of Us Are Dead Season 2' is finally coming to an end. Almost four years after the Korean zombie thriller exploded onto Netflix and gripped viewers worldwide, the survivors of Hyosan High School are gearing up for another round of chaos and survival. What began as a high school outbreak story in early 2022 became one of the platform’s biggest global hits, pulling in hundreds of millions of viewing hours and leaving fans desperate for answers. Now the second season has wrapped filming and moved into post-production, bringing the story closer than it has been in a long time. Familiar faces are returning, new characters are joining the fray, and the series is set to shift its focus in a darker, more unexpected direction.When and where does season 2 arrive?'All of Us Are Dead Season 2' is coming exclusively to Netflix, the same home that launched the first season in January 2022. An official release date has not been locked in yet, but reports point toward an early 2027 premiere, most likely sometime in January or February. On 6th June, 2022, Netflix confirmed season 2 of the series, which was on the first day of Geeked Week. Park Ji-hu, Yoon Chan-young, Cho Yi-hyun, and Lomon were delivering the news in a short video.According to What’s on Netflix, filming for the new season wrapped in February 2026, and the project is now deep in post-production. Production plans pushed the schedule later than many expected, and the show even missed Netflix’s announced Korean slate for 2026. Still, the recent progress has given fans a clearer picture after years of silence.Looking back at the chaos of season 1Season 1 dropped viewers straight into the middle of a nightmare. A zombie virus tore through Hyosan High School and the surrounding city, which resulted in the trapping of a group of ordinary teenagers inside the building with the infected. The students had to fight for survival while dealing with the virus, military responses, and the hard choices that come when society collapses around them. The series mixed intense action with emotional character moments, and audiences responded in a big way. It racked up roughly 560.78 million viewing hours in its first 28 days, cementing its place as one of Netflix’s strongest Korean original hits. The cliffhangers and unanswered questions, especially around certain key characters, left people wanting more the moment the final episode ended.Who’s coming back, and who’s new?Netflix Korea’s July 2025 announcement has confirmed that four of the main cast members are returning. Park Ji-hu will reprise her role as Nam On-jo, Yoon Chan-young is back as Lee Cheong-san, Cho Yi-hyun returns as Choi Nam-ra, and Lomon will again play Lee Su-hyeok. Their characters carried much of the emotional weight in the first season, so their return is a big deal for fans who invested in their stories. The new season also brings in fresh faces. Lee Min-jae joins as Yong Ma-ru, Kim Si-eun appears as So Ju-ran, Yoon Ga-i plays Lee Jong-ah, and Roh Jae-won takes on the role of Han Doo-seok, a team leader with South Korea’s National Intelligence Service. A few actors from the original cast, including Lee Eun-saem, Ha Seung-ri, and Lim Jae-hyeok, have not been officially confirmed yet, so their status remains unclear for now.What the new season might exploreDirector Lee Jae-kyu gave an early hint about the direction back in February 2022. Speaking to Korean media, including Insight, he said, “If season 1 was about humans surviving, season 2 will be about zombies surviving.” That single line has fuelled fresh excitement among fans of the series for years. It suggests the sequel will dig deeper and unravel how the world has changed in the years since the initial outbreak. Korean outlets such as Sports Kyunghyang have described season 2 as expanding from the high school to “university and downtown Seoul.”With the core group of survivors returning and new characters entering the mix, including someone from the intelligence service, the story looks ready to expand beyond the high school walls. Expect more questions about what happens after the initial chaos settles, how society tries to rebuild or control the threat, and whether the survivors can truly escape the consequences of what they lived through. After almost four years, the wait is nearly over. Fans who stuck with the story through the long gap finally have a clearer path forward, and the next chapter of All of Us Are Dead is shaping up to be every bit as intense as the first.

articles.title: Delhi court orders release of CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A special executive magistrate (SEM) court in Delhi on Wednesday accepted the surety bonds of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A special executive magistrate (SEM) court in Delhi on Wednesday accepted the surety bonds of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka and ordered their release, officials said.The court said they may be released from jail if they are not in custody in any other case. The order came after Delhi Police sought a three-day extension of their judicial custody.The two leaders have been in police custody for 7 days.On their way back, Saurav Das in the brief interaction with media responded to the court's order saying, "Truth has prevailed."The CJP founder and leader Abhijeet Dipke shared his reaction to the court's release order. Taking to his X account, Dipke shared a clip from the climax scene of Shah Rukh Khan's movie Chak De India.High court asks activists to pursue alternative remedyEarlier in the day, Das and Ranka challenged the extension of their custody before the Delhi high court. The court asked them to await the SEM's decision and approach the appropriate appellate or revisional forum if their grievance persisted. The activists subsequently withdrew their plea.Delhi HC also questioned why they had invoked its writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution when an alternative legal remedy was available.“Your second incident. You are a person who has actually broken a bond. Your remedy actually lies in revision,” the court observed while hearing the challenge to the SEM's October 19 order.The bench also questioned whether authorities could impose stricter surety conditions following an alleged second breach of a peace bond.“Once you have broken peace for the second time, are the authorities not entitled to insist upon everything?” the court asked.The court further expressed concern that breaching barricades at Jantar Mantar could encourage others to violate prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).“The two petitioners here are at the forefront. When you go and break a barricade, the chances of 10 or 20 more people in violation of 163 are very high,” the court observed.Advocate Abhik Chimni, appearing for the petitioners, argued that the SEM lacked jurisdiction to extend their custody and that their sureties had been wrongly rejected. The High Court clarified that it had not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case before permitting the withdrawal of the plea.CJP leaders detained after Jantar Mantar protestDas and Ranka were initially remanded to five days of judicial custody on October 14 after being detained for allegedly entering Jantar Mantar, which had been denotified as a designated protest site, and violating peace bonds. Their custody was extended by two days on October 19.The activists challenged the extension under Sections 126 and 170 of the BNSS, arguing that their continued detention was illegal and that the allegations did not establish an imminent threat to peace and tranquillity.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Festival for everyone’: A pandal with reserved viewing for differently abled, elderly
articles.summary: Ghaziabad Vaishali Durga Puja pandal reserves viewing for disabled and elderly visitors, offers wheelchair help, promoting inclusive “festival for everyone.”
articles.body: Ghaziabad: A Durga Puja committee in Vaishali has made accessibility the theme of its 21st celebration, with reserved viewing spaces and wheelchair assistance for persons with disabilities and senior citizens.Sarbojanin Shri Shri Kali Puja Samiti (SSSKPS) began its puja at Rachna Park in Sector 3-A on Friday under the theme “Sarbojonin Pujo”, or a festival for everyone. In earlier years, the pandal was not wheelchair accessible, and persons with disabilities and senior citizens struggled to get a clear view of the Durga idol or reach the front for darshan.“We want everyone to enjoy the puja with dignity, without any discrimination,” said cultural secretary Somanath Das, explaining the idea behind the theme.Para powerlifter Rajkumari, an Asian Games bronze medallist who inaugurated the puja, said such efforts address a gap that often keeps persons with disabilities from public events.“In India, most places are not disabled-friendly, unlike in other countries. You feel more disabled because of the lack of infrastructure,” she said. “It’s particularly difficult to be a wheelchair user because most places lack ramps.”She added that the absence of basic facilities often forces people with disabilities to miss out on social gatherings. “We want to feel included too. I have seen friends skipping out on fun because there are no ramps for wheelchair users,” she said.Kumari welcomed the committee’s effort and urged the govt to extend the approach beyond festivals. “It’s great to see events including this kind of infrastructure,” she said. “I want the Indian govt to ensure every public space is disabled-friendly.”The initiative was inspired by UNESCO’s campaign to make festivals more accessible. Its guidelines emphasise not just barrier-free infrastructure, such as ramps and accessible pathways, but also inclusive programming, emergency preparedness, trained volunteers and a change in public attitudes towards disability.Somanath said the committee had considered installing ramps and rails, but practical constraints meant it could not address every accessibility concern. The aim, he said, was to make the space as accessible as possible and encourage people to think differently about inclusion.“Durga Puja is a festival because we enjoy it. It goes beyond rituals,” he said, adding that inclusiveness was its main essence. The committee hopes the initiative will send a wider message about acceptance and the need to ensure everyone can participate in community celebrations.The theme builds on the committee’s earlier social initiatives. Last year, its focus was women’s empowerment. This year, it has extended financial assistance of Rs 21,000 to Anandamayee Mental Disability and Handicapped Society in Kolkata, which works for the welfare of children with special needs.The committee also describes its idea of inclusion as extending across religious lines. Somanath said members of different faiths are part of the organising team. Singer Runa Hussain is scheduled to perform on Navami as part of the cultural programme.The celebrations include community welfare activities, with a health check-up camp and a dental camp on Sunday and free distribution of spectacles by a local shop. Daily pujas and rituals will continue throughout the festival. articles.summary: Rescued nilgai calf found in Kundri range and saved by a villager was rehabilitated and released in Palamu Tiger Reserve’s Garu range, officials said.
articles.body: Daltonganj: A nilgai calf rescued from Kundri range of the Medininagar forest division has been released in Garu range of Palamu Tiger Reserve (PTR), forest officials said on Wednesday.According to officials, PTR is not a natural habitat for nilgai, but it was considered the safest available forest area for rehabilitating the abandoned animal. articles.title: Tourists, commuters stranded as landslide disrupts traffic on Pollachi-Valparai Ghat Road for several hours
articles.summary: COIMBATORE: Heavy rain on Tuesday night triggered a landslide, sending massive boulders rolling onto the Pollachi-Valparai Ghat Road and bringing traffic
articles.body: COIMBATORE: Heavy rain on Tuesday night triggered a landslide, sending massive boulders rolling onto the Pollachi-Valparai Ghat Road and bringing traffic to a standstill for more than 15 hours, leaving scores of tourists and commuters stranded. The disruption continued into Wednesday, with officials deploying heavy machinery to remove the boulders and restore traffic.The landslide occurred near the third hairpin bend on the ghat road around 8pm on Tuesday, with two giant boulders rolling onto the carriageway and damaging a section of the road. The impact left the stretch impassable even for two-wheelers, cutting off the main road link between Pollachi and Valparai. No vehicles were passing at the time of the incident, averting a possible major accident. The road was cleared around 5pm on Wednesday, after almost 21 hours.According to an official from the district administration, the size of the boulders made their removal difficult. The official said, “Because of the size, personnel from the highways department, police and fire and rescue services had to carry out work throughout the night. We could not allow vehicle movement until the road was cleared, considering the safety of passengers. Initially, we attempted to remove the boulders with earthmovers but failed. So, we had to use rock drills to make them small pieces and then remove them.”The disruption left tourists returning from Valparai waiting for hours, with some reportedly facing a shortage of food and drinking water. Families with children were among those stranded near the Aliyar checkpost.Vehicles travelling uphill from Pollachi were stopped, while those descending from Valparai were held back until the road could be cleared.A tourist from Hosur said, “My three friends and I came to Valparai on Monday and were returning on Tuesday night. We had no alternative road and had to wait until the road was cleared. District officials could have provided some assistance, at least to provide water or food for those waiting throughout the night. More than 100 people have been left stranded including children and families.”The road closure affected the movement of essential supplies, including milk.Aliyar recorded 96.8mm of rain until Wednesday morning, according to the Tamil Nadu State Disaster Management Authority’s report. articles.title: Two arrested for killing a man in Koderma
articles.summary: Koderma police arrest wife Kiran Devi and Sunil Thakur for Naresh Thakur’s murder; body found in abandoned stone mine, lethal injection alleged.
articles.body: Koderma: Police have arrested two persons, including the wife of the deceased, in connection with the murder of a 40-year-old man whose body was recovered from an abandoned stone mine in Koderma on Oct 17.The deceased, identified as Naresh Thakur, a resident of Chauparan in Hazaribag district, was found in an abandoned stone mine under the Nawalshahi police station area. Following the recovery of the body, a case was registered and a special investigation team (SIT) led by Nawalshahi officer-in-charge Suman Kumar was constituted by Koderma SP Kumar Shivasish.Addressing the media on Wednesday, the SP said police arrested Kiran Devi, wife of the deceased, and Sunil Thakur, a resident of Behradih in Koderma.According to the SP, Kiran Devi and Sunil Thakur were allegedly in a relationship while living in Kolkata and had conspired to eliminate Naresh. Investigations revealed that when Naresh was passing through Koderma railway station while unwell, Sunil persuaded him to visit his clinic in Nawalshahi on the pretext of providing medical treatment.Police alleged that Sunil administered a lethal injection to Naresh, resulting in his death. After allegedly consulting Kiran on the phone, Sunil packed the body in a plastic bag, transported it on his motorcycle during the night and dumped it in the abandoned stone mine.Police have seized the motorcycle and mobile phone allegedly used in the commission of the crime. Further investigation is underway, said the SP.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Dr Reddy’s Labs gets CDSCO nod for Zytorvi use in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
articles.summary: Dr Reddy’s gets CDSCO approval for Zytorvi (toripalimab) with chemo as first-line treatment for advanced ESCC in adults, backed by Phase 3 data.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Dr Reddy’s Laboratories said on Wednesday that the Indian drug regulator has approved Zytorvi, its toripalimab, with cisplatin and paclitaxel as a first-line treatment for adults with unresectable advanced, recurrent or metastatic oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC).The approval by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), under the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI), gives Zytorvi its second indication in the country after recurrent or metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Dr Reddy’s had licensed toripalimab from Shanghai Junshi Biosciences in 2023 for development and commercialisation across 21 countries.The company said the Indian indication does not require patient selection based on PD-L1 expression, aligning with European approval for first-line ESCC. Toripalimab is also approved by regulators including US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA), European Medicines Agency (EMA) and UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (UK-MHRA).The CDSCO approval was supported by the Phase 3 JUPITER-06 trial, where toripalimab plus chemotherapy cut the risk of disease progression or death by 42% versus chemotherapy alone. Median overall survival was 17.7 months, compared with 12.9 months, the company said.MV Ramana, CEO, global generics, Dr Reddy’s Laboratories, said after the approval of Zytorvi for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, this second indication marks an important step in extending the reach of immunotherapy to patients with advanced ESCC and gives physicians an additional first-line treatment option for appropriate patients.Oesophageal cancer was India’s fourth leading cause of cancer-related death in 2024, representing about 8.1% of cancer deaths.
